newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir loses power after renewed navigation problem.
newsitem.headline: Mir loses power after renewed navigation problem.

text.p: The Mir space station lost some electric power overnight after an unexplained problem hit the system that keeps the orbiting craft's solar batteries lined up on the Sun, Mission Control officials said on Thursday.

Valentin Udaloi, the deputy head of Mission Control outside Moscow, told reporters the three-man Russian-American crew were trying to correct the problem -- which has dogged Mir since an accident on June 25 by using the station's Soyuz spacecraft.
A second official told reporters: "We've already had similar cases. It's not serious but it is unpleasant." A third Mission Control worker said: "I think it'll last a day or two."
Further details on the problem, which struck around midnight GMT, were not available. Reporters saw increased activity among ground specialists at Mission Control in the suburb of Korolyov.

Mir lost up to half its electric power on June 25 after the crew had to seal off one of its modules, including four major solar batteries, following a collision with an unmanned craft that punctured the Spektr unit. The cosmonauts are due to enter the airless module to restore some power cables late next week.

Meanwhile Mir has suffered repeated failures in the gyroscopic system that keeps its remaining solar panels lined up on the Sun as the craft hurtles round the Earth in orbit. That creates a vicious circle, depriving the station of further power and hence making it even more difficult to reorient it. The problem has been solved in the past by firing rocket motors.
